text:
jess: heads up — over the last 20m we saw internal-api 5xx spike. traces point at long DNS resolves and a handful of SERVFAILs. svc lookups timing out ~1s-3s and then downstream 504s. anyone else seeing this?
jess: sample from app logs: "dns_lookup internal-api.default.svc.cluster.local timeout=2200ms err=SERVFAIL"
matt: seeing it in grafana too — resolver p99 jumped from 40ms -> 1.8s at 02:12 UTC. is this CoreDNS or node-local-dns? any recent rollouts?
sarah: CoreDNS had a canary config bump 02:05 that adjusted EDNS/UDP size and enabled a new cache plugin. deploy-bot showed canary -> stable at 02:10.
ryan: ran a quick endpoints check — some endpoints for internal-api went empty for a few seconds around 02:11, then came back. pasted output: 
```
# kubectl get endpoints internal-api -n prod -o jsonpath='{.subsets}'
[]
# 02:11:14
```
matt: interesting. I also ran a dig during the spike: 
```
$ dig +nocmd internal-api.default.svc.cluster.local @10.96.0.10 +short
; <<>> DiG 9.11.3 <<>> ...
;; Truncated, retrying in TCP.
;; ->>HEADER<<- opcode: QUERY, status: SERVFAIL, tc: 1
```
jess: tcpdump from a node shows lots of DNS TCP fallbacks and repeated SYNs to port 53, and intermittent RSTs. hard to correlate but looks like UDP responses were too big and caused truncation + TCP fallback stress.
sarah: FYI — infra team enabled jumbo frames on some RDMA-backed GPU nodes last week (9000 MTU) to reduce RDMA segmenting. control-plane hosts still at 1500. could be path MTU mismatch on our overlay.
ryan: confirming: tcpdump shows UDP responses with EDNS size ~4096, then node-local-dns returns SERVFAIL shortly after. hypothesis: large UDP replies get dropped on some east-west paths -> client falls back to TCP -> connection spikes -> higher latency and some requests time out.
matt: that fits with the empty endpoints snapshot — kube-proxy healthchecks may have failed during the DNS hiccup causing transient endpoint lists. also node-local negative caching might be holding SERVFAILs for 10s. can we reduce negative TTL?
sarah: immediate mitigations: 1) roll coreDNS Corefile change that raised EDNS UDP size (rollback canary) 2) limit UDP response size from CoreDNS to 1232 (avoid fragmentation) 3) bump node-local-dns replicas + reduce negative cache TTL to 1s.
jess: +1 to rollback. can we patch CoreDNS quickly? what are cluster-wide risks?
ryan: low-risk rolling restart of coredns/stable -> do canary rollback only, not whole cluster. I'll run the rollback and keep a 15m watch.
infra-bot: deploy-bot: rolling restart started for deployment/coredns (3 -> 3) at 02:36 UTC by ryan.
matt: I'll add a temporary datapoint: set CoreDNS `max_udp_size 1232` in Corefile and reload. that should stop truncation + TCP fallback under current MTU mix.
sarah: long-term action items: audit MTU config across RDMA/GPU hosts + overlay, decide on a single canonical MTU (likely 1500 or document jumbo everywhere), and add e2e test that sends EDNS-large responses across AZs.
jess: thanks team. ryan — please post outcome. I'll keep postmortem stub and collect traces for the last 2 hours.
ryan: rollback completed at 02:39, monitoring now. initial graphs look improved, resolver p99 back to ~50ms. will leave watch for 30m.
sarah: opened infra ticket INF-4527 to track MTU audit and node-local-dns config change. assigned to me.
matt: created a shortrun alert for DNS truncated responses > 10/min in prod channel.
jess: confirmed fewer 5xxs after rollback. leaving this thread open until postmortem. :thumbsup:
